Named customers

Organisations named in public sources as using this vendor’s tracked products, strongest evidence first.

No named customer could be confirmed from public sources. Vendors often cannot name bank customers, so this is not a finding about adoption.

How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Reputation

Adverse items are attributed to their sources and need one primary source or two independent ones before they are published.

Reputation
Regulatory actionsItaly's Garante announced on 2025-01-30 that it had ordered DeepSeek's two operating companies to limit processing of Italian users' data and opened an investigation, stating that the companies' reply was wholly insufficient. The US Department of Homeland Security published on 2026-10-20 an order dated 2026-07-24 excluding DeepSeek products from federal civilian agency procurement and systems, stating that its servers are in China and that Chinese law gives government bodies broad access to company infrastructure. CISA, the NSA and the FBI published an advisory on 2026-09-08 alleging that DeepSeek and five other China-based companies distilled US companies' models in breach of terms of use. NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation published an evaluation on 2025-09-30 reporting that DeepSeek models were more susceptible to agent hijacking and jailbreaking than US reference models. The Berlin data protection commissioner published a notice to Apple and Google describing the DeepSeek app as illegal content in June 2025. Global News and The Canadian Press reported on 2025-02-07 that the app was restricted on Canadian government mobile devices managed by Shared Services Canada. A Reuters factbox of 2026-01-07 also lists public-sector bans in the Czech Republic, the Netherlands, Australia and Taiwan and a download suspension in South Korea that was later lifted; those were not verified against the issuing bodies in this session. No measure by a UK authority was found.   2. How many employees does DeepSeek have, and how many work on API operations, security and customer support?

  3. Has DeepSeek made any workforce reductions in the last 24 months, and what is its current headcount trend?
    Workforce reductions are an early sign of financial stress.

    Loss of large customers can indicate product or trust problems.
  5. Have there been any departures, investigations or disputes involving DeepSeek's senior leadership in the last 24 months?
    Leadership instability or misconduct affects vendor reliability.

Timeline

  1. 2026-09-08 · regulatory action DeepSeekAlibaba Cloud
    US agencies' advisory alleges model distillation campaigns by DeepSeek, Alibaba and four other firms

    CISA, the NSA and the FBI published advisory AA26-251A on 8 September 2026, which stated that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun and Z.AI had conducted high-volume distillation of US AI companies' models since at least late 2024 in breach of the providers' terms of use. The advisory stated that DeepSeek used the outputs to train its R1 and V3 models and that Alibaba used them to improve its Qwen models. These are the agencies' allegations; no response from either company was found in this session. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, with NSA and FBI (regulator or standards body, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-07-24 · regulatory action DeepSeek
    US DHS orders DeepSeek products excluded and removed from federal civilian agency systems

    The US Department of Homeland Security published in the Federal Register on 20 October 2026 notice of Exclusion and Removal Order #2026-01, dated 24 July 2026 and issued under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act. The order directs federal civilian executive agencies to exclude Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd and affiliated entities from procurements and to remove DeepSeek products, and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations, from their information technology, with exceptions available on request. The order states that DeepSeek's servers are located in China and that use could result in transfer of sensitive data there. It does not apply to private companies. U.S. Department of Homeland Security (Federal Register) (regulator or standards body, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)TechCrunch (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  3. 2026-07-17 · funding DeepSeek
    DeepSeek's first external funding round reported at about 50 billion yuan

    Caixin Global reported on 17 July 2026, citing a regulatory filing by a listed company that invested indirectly, that DeepSeek raised about 50 billion yuan in its first external round at a post-money valuation above 350 billion yuan, with Tencent and CATL among the investors. The Next Web, citing Reuters, reported on 16 June 2026 that founder Liang Wenfeng was to contribute the largest share. DeepSeek did not announce the round on the pages reviewed. Caixin Global (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)The Next Web (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  4. 2026-04-24 · launch DeepSeek
    DeepSeek releases V4 models on its API and sets retirement date for legacy model names

    DeepSeek's API change log records the release of DeepSeek-V4-Pro and V4-Flash on 24 April 2026 through OpenAI-format and Anthropic-format interfaces, with the legacy names deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner to be discontinued three months later. DeepSeek (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  5. 2025-06-27 · regulatory action DeepSeek
    Berlin data protection commissioner notifies Apple and Google of DeepSeek app as illegal content

    The Berlin Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information published a press release in June 2025 stating that it had notified Apple and Google in Germany of the DeepSeek app as illegal content. Reuters reported in a factbox dated 7 January 2026 that the German commissioner had asked the two companies to remove the app from their stores over data safety concerns. Only the title of the regulator's PDF could be read in this session; the legal reasoning was not reviewed. Berliner Beauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit (regulator or standards body, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)Reuters (carried by Insurance Journal) (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  6. 2025-02-06 · regulatory action DeepSeek
    Canada restricts DeepSeek chatbot on some federal government devices

    Reported by Global News on 7 February 2025: an email from the chief information officer of the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat said the DeepSeek application was restricted on government mobile devices managed by Shared Services Canada as a precaution, citing serious privacy concerns about collection and retention of personal information, and recommended that other departments consider blocking the application and website. The Canadian Press, carried by CTV News the same day, reported the restriction on some government phones. The memo itself was not found on a government site. Global News (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)CTV News (The Canadian Press) (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  7. 2025-01-30 · regulatory action DeepSeek
    Italian data protection authority orders limitation of DeepSeek's processing of Italian users' data

    The Garante per la protezione dei dati personali announced on 30 January 2025 that it had urgently ordered Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence and Beijing DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence to limit processing of Italian users' data, with immediate effect, and had opened an investigation. The authority stated that the companies' reply, which said they did not operate in Italy and that European law did not apply to them, was wholly insufficient. Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (regulator or standards body, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  8. 2025-01-29 · security incident DeepSeek
    Researchers report a publicly accessible DeepSeek database containing chat histories and API keys

    Reported by TechCrunch and The Register on 30 January 2025, citing research published by Wiz on 29 January 2025: an unauthenticated ClickHouse database belonging to DeepSeek was reachable from the internet and held more than a million log entries including chat history, API keys and backend details. Wiz stated that DeepSeek secured the database promptly after being notified. TechCrunch reported that it was not known whether anyone else had accessed it and that DeepSeek did not respond to a request for comment.
